mainTopic: The four-day inspection of the תמיד lambs, the music of the מקדש (trumpets, cymbal, לוים singers and boys), and the opening of the פרק on cases of ערכין that are lenient and stringent
overview: This amud finishes the explanation of why the מקדש kept six inspected lambs. Each תמיד lamb needs four days of inspection, following בן בג בג, who learns this from the קרבן פסח. The משנה's word 'כדי' (enough for) confirms that שבת and ראש השנה are only a memory aid. The גמרא then gives sources for the music rules: trumpets may be added up to 120, and only one cymbal is played, since a pair of cymbals counts as one instrument. A new משנה says at least twelve לוים stand on the דוכן. Young boys may join only by singing. רבי אליעזר בן יעקב adds that the boys do not count toward the twelve and stand on the ground. The גמרא explains that the twelve match the twelve minimum instruments. It also shows that the נבל and כנור are two separate instruments, even according to רבי יהודה, and explains why the boys were called צוערי. After the הדרן, the next פרק opens with four areas of law where a fixed amount can be lenient or stringent. The גמרא begins asking whether that משנה's words 'in ישראל' go against רבי מאיר's view that a גוי can be valued, and the answer continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The lambs are inspected four days, and the view is בן בג בג's
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its explanation of the six lambs: they are inspected four days before slaughter. It says this follows the opinion of בן בג בג.
steps.simpleTranslation: The six lambs are the ones inspected in the Chamber of the Lambs for four days before slaughter. Whose opinion is this? It is בן בג בג's.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes its answer about why the משנה needs six lambs: each lamb must be checked for four days before it is used. Then it names whose opinion this is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A תמיד is brought every morning and evening, so two lambs are used each day. Keeping six on hand means there are always lambs that have already had their full four days of inspection. Not everyone requires four days, so the גמרא points out that this explanation follows בן בג בג.

Inspection, checking the animal for a blemish (מום)

steps.title: בן בג בג learns the four-day check from the קרבן פסח
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא brings בן בג בג's source. The word 'guarding' appears both for the תמיד and for the קרבן פסח. So the תמיד needs four days of inspection, just like the פסח.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it was taught: בן בג בג says, how do we know the תמיד needs inspection four days before slaughter? The פסוק says about the תמיד, 'You shall guard to offer to Me in its time.' About the פסח it says, 'It shall be for you a guarding until the fourteenth day of the first month.' Just as the פסח needs four days of inspection, so does the תמיד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא to prove that בן בג בג really holds the four-day rule. It also shows where he learns it from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסח lamb was taken on the 10th of ניסן and kept until the 14th, which is four days of watching it. The תמיד's פסוק uses a similar word, 'תשמרו' (guard). So בן בג בג applies the פסח's four days of watching to the תמיד as well.

keyTerms.meaning: The daily offering, one lamb in the morning and one in the afternoon

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the whole explanation of the six lambs in the משנה. Without the four-day rule, the number six would have no reason.

steps.title: The משנה's word 'enough' supports this reading
steps.stepSummary: The משנה says the six lambs are 'enough for' שבת, not 'for' שבת. That wording shows שבת is only a measuring stick, which supports the four-day explanation.
steps.simpleTranslation: The wording is also exact. The משנה says 'enough for שבת' and does not say 'for שבת.' Learn from this that the explanation is right.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points to a small word in the משנה, 'כדי' (enough for), to back up its explanation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the משנה meant the lambs were actually used for שבת and ראש השנה, it would say 'for שבת.' Saying 'enough for' shows that שבת and ראש השנה only describe the number of days the lambs would last. So the real point is having enough lambs on hand, already inspected.

keyTerms.meaning: 'It is also exact,' meaning the wording of the source supports what was just said

steps.whatToRemember: The six lambs in the משנה are about keeping lambs already inspected for four days (בן בג בג). שבת and ראש השנה are only a way to remember the number. The word 'כדי' in the משנה proves this.

steps.title: Two trumpets and more, but up to how many?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה: at least two trumpets, and more may be added. It asks what the upper limit is.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: 'From two trumpets, and one may add, etc.' Up to how many?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line of the משנה about trumpets. It sets up a question that the next step will answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gives a minimum of two trumpets and allows adding more. The גמרא wants to know whether there is a maximum.

keyTerms.meaning: Trumpets blown by the כהנים in the מקדש
And one may add more

phrases.english: "From two trumpets, and one may add, etc."

steps.title: רב הונא: up to 120 trumpets
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא answers that one may add trumpets up to 120. The source is a פסוק about the 120 כהנים who blew trumpets at the dedication of שלמה's מקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said (and some say רב זבדי said in the name of רב הונא): up to 120. As it says: 'And with them were 120 כהנים blowing trumpets.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question: the limit is 120 trumpets. It brings a פסוק as proof.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The number comes from a real event, the dedication of the first מקדש, where 120 כהנים blew trumpets. Since that many were used, 120 is taken as the upper limit. The double attribution simply shows two versions of who reported רב הונא's teaching.

steps.title: Where do we learn that only one cymbal was played?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about the harps and the single cymbal, and asks for the source.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: at least nine harps, and the cymbal alone. Where do we learn this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next line of the משנה and asks for a source. This sets up רב אסי's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said that more harps may be added, but the cymbal stays at one. The גמרא wants a source for that special limit on the cymbal.

steps.title: רב אסי: אסף alone played the cymbals
steps.stepSummary: רב אסי brings a פסוק that names one person, אסף, as the cymbal player.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אסי said: the פסוק says, 'And אסף with the cymbals, sounding aloud.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב אסי answers with a פסוק that names one person who played the cymbals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק lists many לוים on other instruments, but it gives the cymbals only to אסף. So only one cymbal player is needed, with no extra players added.

steps.title: But cymbals come as two
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: the word 'cymbals' is plural, so there were two, not one.
steps.simpleTranslation: But 'cymbals' means two!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the משנה's wording, which calls the cymbal one instrument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק uses the plural 'cymbals', which suggests two pieces. So how can the משנה say there was only one cymbal?

keyTerms.meaning: Two (Aramaic)

phrases.english: Cymbals are two!

steps.title: Two cymbals played by one person count as one
steps.stepSummary: Two cymbals do one job and one person plays them, so they are counted as one instrument.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since they do one job, and one man plays them, they are called one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The pair of cymbals is counted as one instrument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There really are two metal pieces. But they make one sound together, and one person bangs them against each other. So the משנה counts them as one instrument.

steps.whatToRemember: Only one cymbal was played, based on the פסוק about אסף. A pair of cymbals counts as one instrument because one person plays them as a single action.

steps.title: משנה: at least twelve לוים, and boys only sing
steps.stepSummary: There are at least twelve לוים on the דוכן, and more may be added. A young boy may enter the עזרה only to sing with his mouth, not to play instruments.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are no fewer than twelve לוים standing on the דוכן, and more may be added without limit. A minor may enter the עזרה to serve only when the לוים are singing. The boys did not play the lyre or the harp; they sang with their mouths, to add sweetness to the music.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה gives the minimum number of לוים singers. It also explains when and how young boys took part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Like the instruments, the singers have a minimum and no maximum. A young boy may enter the עזרה only during the singing, and only to sing. His high voice adds flavor to the music.

keyTerms.meaning: The platform where the לוים stood and sang
The courtyard of the בית המקדש

steps.title: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב: the boys were not counted and stood below
steps.stepSummary: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says the boys do not count toward the twelve and do not go up on the דוכן. They stood on the ground and were called the junior לוים.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says: The boys are not counted toward the number, and they do not go up on the דוכן. They stood on the ground, with their heads between the legs of the לוים, and they were called the junior לוים.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with רבי אליעזר בן יעקב, who adds limits on the boys who sang.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The boys do not count toward the minimum of twelve, so you still need twelve adult לוים. They stood on the ground below the platform, so their heads came up to the legs of the לוים standing above them.

keyTerms.meaning: The count, the required number

steps.whatToRemember: At least twelve לוים stand on the דוכן. Boys may join in the singing, but according to רבי אליעזר בן יעקב they do not count toward the twelve and they stand on the ground.

steps.title: What does the number twelve match?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the twelve לוים in the משנה correspond to.

steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gave the number twelve without a reason. The גמרא wants to know what the number is based on.

steps.title: רב פפא: twelve matches the twelve minimum instruments
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says the twelve match nine harps, two lyres and one cymbal, and brings a פסוק that mentions twelve.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: They match nine harps, two lyres and one cymbal, as it says: 'He and his sons and his brothers were twelve.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא explains that the twelve singers match the minimum number of instruments. He supports this with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier משנה gave minimums of nine harps, two lyres and one cymbal, which add up to twelve. The singers match the instruments, and the פסוק in דברי הימים also speaks of groups of twelve.

steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה and asks for its source. This sets up רבי יוחנן's answer in the next step.

steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says ישוע stood "with his sons" while leading the music. This shows that young sons may join the adults when there is singing. It does not show they may do other kinds of עבודה.

steps.title: The משנה seems to treat the נבל and כנור as two instruments
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה that the boys did not play נבל or כנור, and notes that this treats them as separate instruments.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said the boys did not play the lyre or the harp, only sang with their mouths. So does this mean a lyre and a harp are two separate things?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes another line of the משנה and points out what it implies: the נבל and the כנור are two different instruments. This sets up the challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By listing the two names one after the other, the משנה seems to treat them as two kinds of instruments. The גמרא raises this so it can check whether everyone agrees.

steps.title: Does the משנה disagree with רבי יהודה? The seven-string harp
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests the משנה goes against רבי יהודה, who teaches in a ברייתא that the כנור of the מקדש had seven strings.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say our משנה does not follow רבי יהודה? A ברייתא teaches that רבי יהודה says: the harp of the מקדש had seven strings, as it says, "fullness of joy is in Your presence." Do not read it as "fullness" (שובע), but as "seven" (שבע).
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא suggests our משנה may disagree with רבי יהודה. It begins quoting his ברייתא, which says the כנור in the מקדש had seven strings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה speaks of one כנור whose number of strings changes over time. As his teaching continues, this will suggest that a כנור and a נבל might really be the same instrument. If so, the משנה's listing them separately would not fit his view.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say? (a suggestion the גמרא tests)
Strings of an instrument
Do not read it as... but as... (reading a word differently to teach something)

steps.confusionAlert: Seven strings by itself is not yet the problem. The challenge only becomes clear with the last part of his teaching, the ten strings, where the פסוק mentions נבל and כנור together.

phrases.english: Shall we say that our mishna is not in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda?
As it is taught in a baraita: Rabbi Yehuda says:

phrases.aramaic: כִּנּוֹר שֶׁל מִקְדָּשׁ שֶׁל שִׁבְעַת נִימִין הָיָה,
phrases.english: The harp of the Temple was of seven strings,
as it is stated: "Fullness of joy is in Your presence",
phrases.notes: תהלים 16:11. "In Your presence" points to the מקדש.

phrases.english: Do not read "fullness" but "seven."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the implication from step 16 to suggest a conflict with רבי יהודה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's treatment of נבל and כנור as separate instruments.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה describes one instrument whose number of strings grows over time. The פסוק he uses for the final stage links נבל and כנור together, so it seems he sees them as one instrument. That would not fit the משנה.

steps.title: In the days of משיח the harp will have eight strings
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה continues: the כנור of the days of משיח will have eight strings, learned from "על השמינית."
steps.simpleTranslation: And the harp of the days of משיח will have eight strings, as it says: "For the leader, on the eighth." This means on the eighth string.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא of רבי יהודה continues. The harp will gain an eighth string in the days of משיח.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads "השמינית" (the eighth) as an eighth string. This adds a second stage to his picture of one harp that keeps getting more strings.

keyTerms.meaning: The days of משיח
Eighth
A string

phrases.english: And that of the days of the Messiah has eight,
as it is stated: "For the leader, on the eighth",
phrases.notes: תהלים 12:1

phrases.english: on the eighth string.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא of רבי יהודה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כנור of the days of משיח will have eight strings.

steps.title: In עולם הבא the harp will have ten strings
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה finishes: in עולם הבא the instrument will have ten strings, from a פסוק that mentions עשור, נבל and כנור together.
steps.simpleTranslation: And that of עולם הבא will have ten strings, as it says: "Upon a ten-stringed instrument and upon the lyre, with a solemn sound upon the harp."
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא ends with the third stage: ten strings in עולם הבא. This is where the challenge against the משנה becomes sharp.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ten-string פסוק mentions the נבל and the כנור in one line. This seems to show that רבי יהודה treats the growing כנור and the נבל as the same instrument. That is why the גמרא thought the משנה, which lists them separately, does not follow him.

keyTerms.meaning: The World to Come
A ten-stringed instrument
A solemn, thoughtful sound

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה: the harp has 7 strings in the מקדש, 8 in the days of משיח, and 10 in עולם הבא. The גמרא suspects that by his view נבל and כנור are one instrument, against our משנה. Step 21 answers this.

phrases.english: That of the World-to-Come has ten,
as it is stated: "With an instrument of ten strings and with the lyre,
phrases.notes: תהלים 92:4, from the מזמור for שבת.

phrases.english: with a solemn sound upon the harp."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא of רבי יהודה that supports the challenge in step 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The instrument of עולם הבא will have ten strings, from a פסוק linking עשור, נבל and כנור.

steps.title: A second verse: the ten-stringed instrument of the new song
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה's ברייתא brings a second פסוק about a ten-stringed נבל and a 'new song.' This completes the challenge against our משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And another פסוק says: 'Give thanks to ה׳ with the harp, sing to Him with a ten-stringed lyre. Sing to Him a new song!'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא of רבי יהודה adds one more פסוק to prove that the instrument of עולם הבא will have ten strings. Here the גמרא's challenge against our משנה reaches its full strength.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'new song' points to עולם הבא, and the פסוק calls the ten-stringed instrument a נבל. So it looks like for רבי יהודה the כנור and the נבל are one instrument. That goes against our משנה, which lists them as two separate instruments.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And it says': brings an extra פסוק as more proof
Ten (here, ten strings)
A new song, understood as the song of עולם הבא

phrases.english: And it says:
"Give thanks to ה׳ with the harp,
phrases.notes: תהלים 33:2–3

phrases.english: with a ten-stringed lyre sing praises to Him;
sing to Him a new song!"
phrases.notes: The 'new song' is the song of עולם הבא, so this ten-stringed instrument is the one from step 19.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second פסוק to רבי יהודה's proof from step 19, which completes the קשיא from step 17.
steps.raayaObject: In עולם הבא the instrument will have ten strings, and it is called a נבל.

steps.title: Even רבי יהודה agrees they are two instruments
steps.stepSummary: The כנור and נבל really are different instruments. In עולם הבא the כנור will have more strings and a sound as big as a נבל, so it is called a נבל.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say our משנה follows רבי יהודה. In עולם הבא, since the כנור will have more strings, its sound will be big like a נבל, so he calls it a 'נבל.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Our משנה can fit even רבי יהודה's view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה never said the כנור and נבל are the same instrument. In עולם הבא the כנור gets more strings and sounds as full as a נבל, so the פסוק borrows the name 'נבל' for it. In the מקדש they stay two separate instruments, just as our משנה says.

keyTerms.meaning: 'You can even say': the answer fits even the view that seemed to clash
Strings of an instrument
Its sound becomes bigger or fuller

steps.whatToRemember: The כנור and נבל are two different instruments. The ten-stringed כנור of עולם הבא is only called a נבל because it sounds like one.

phrases.english: You can even say it follows Rabbi Yehuda;
in the World to Come,
since its strings will be more,
phrases.notes: 'Its' means the כנור, the harp.

phrases.english: its sound will be big like a lyre,
so he calls it a "lyre."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge built in steps 17–20.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpretation of the source: the name 'נבל' describes how the instrument sounds, not what kind of instrument it is
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה holds that the כנור and נבל are one instrument, which goes against the משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: They are two instruments. The ten-stringed כנור of עולם הבא is called a נבל because its sound is as big as one.

steps.title: The boys' name: צוערי in the משנה, סועדי in a ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes רבי אליעזר בן יעקב's line in the משנה about the boys, then a ברייתא that calls them 'helpers of the לויים.'
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: רבי אליעזר בן יעקב says, the boys are not counted toward the number, etc. A ברייתא teaches: they were called 'the helpers of the לויים.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line in the משנה and sets two names side by side. This prepares the question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה calls the boys 'צוערי הלוים,' but the ברייתא calls them 'סועדי הלוים' (helpers of the לויים). 'Helpers' is easy to understand. That makes the משנה's word stand out as needing an explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: They are not counted toward the minimum number (of twelve לויים)
Helpers or supporters of the לויים

phrases.english: Rabbi Eliezer ben Yaakov says:
They are not counted in the number, etc.
A ברייתא taught:
And they were called the helpers of the Levites.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי אֱלִיעֶזֶר בֶּן יַעֲקֹב אוֹמֵר: אֵין עוֹלִין מִן הַמִּנְיָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: the name the משנה gives the boys.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A ברייתא calls the boys 'סועדי הלוים,' the helpers of the לויים.

steps.title: Why does our משנה call them צוערי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the תנא of our משנה uses the word 'צוערי.'
steps.simpleTranslation: And our תנא, why does he call them 'צוערי'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why our משנה uses a different and odd-sounding name for the boys.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'צוערי' sounds like it comes from צער, pain. The גמרא wants to know what the boys had to do with pain.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Our תנא': the author of our משנה

phrases.english: And our Tanna?
phrases.notes: He's asking: why does our משנה call them 'צוערי' and not 'helpers'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the difference in names shown in step 22.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the משנה calls the boys 'צוערי הלוים.'

steps.title: The boys' high voices pained the grown לויים
steps.stepSummary: The boys could sing high notes that the grown לויים could not reach, so they 'pained' them, which is why they are called צוערי.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since the boys have high voices and the grown men have deep voices, the boys can sing high and the men cannot. So he calls them 'צוערי,' the ones who cause pain.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains that the name 'צוערי' comes from the pain the grown לויים felt.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The boys' high voices could do something the men's deep voices could not. Because the grown לויים could not match them, our משנה's name for the boys is 'צוערי'. This explains why our תנא uses a different name from the ברייתא's 'סועדי'.

keyTerms.meaning: Their voices are thin, meaning high
Their voices are thick, meaning deep
Sing in a high, thin voice
Ones who cause pain (from צַעַר)

steps.whatToRemember: The boys are called צוערי הלוים because their high voices pained the grown לויים, who could not sing that way.

phrases.english: Since these have thin (high) voices,
phrases.notes: 'These' are the boys, and 'those' in the next lines are the grown לויים.

phrases.english: and those have thick (deep) voices,
these sing high
and those cannot sing high,
so he calls them "tzoarei" (pain-causers).
phrases.notes: The word comes from צער, pain. The grown men were pained that they could not sound like the boys.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 23.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The boys' high voices pained the grown לויים, who could not sing that high, so they are called צוערי.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק אין נערכין
steps.stepSummary: The פרק אין נערכין ends with the הדרן formula.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, פרק אין נערכין.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the closing line of the פרק. It is not part of the argument.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן marks that the learning of פרק אין נערכין is finished. It expresses the hope to come back and learn it again.

keyTerms.meaning: 'We will return to you': the formula said at the end of a פרק

phrases.english: We will return to you, "Ein Ne'erachin."
phrases.notes: 'אין נערכין' is the name of this פרק, taken from its opening words.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the פרק after the last explanation.

steps.title: New פרק opens: four areas that can be lenient or stringent
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists four areas of law where a fixed amount can make things easier or harder: ערכין, שדה אחוזה, a שור המועד that killed a slave, and אונס, מפתה, and מוציא שם רע.
steps.simpleTranslation: There are cases in ערכין that are lenient and stringent, in a field of ancestral inheritance that are lenient and stringent, in a forewarned ox that killed a slave that are lenient and stringent, and in a rapist, a seducer, and one who defames his wife that are lenient and stringent.
steps.whatsHappening: A new פרק starts with a list. The משנה names four areas where a fixed Torah amount can turn out lenient in one case and stringent in another.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each item on the list has a set payment in the Torah that does not change with the real value involved. So sometimes the fixed amount is less than the real value (lenient), and sometimes it is more (stringent). The משנה will explain each item one by one, starting with ערכין.

keyTerms.meaning: To be lenient and to be stringent: the same rule can help or hurt depending on the case
A field a family inherited, which has a fixed redemption price when it is consecrated
An ox known to gore, whose owner pays more for its damage
One who forces a girl and one who seduces her; each pays a fixed fine
A husband who falsely accuses his new wife of unfaithfulness

steps.whyThisMatters: This list is the outline for the whole new פרק, which goes through each of these four areas.

phrases.english: MISHNA: There are, regarding valuations,
cases to be lenient and to be stringent;
and regarding an ancestral field, to be lenient and to be stringent;
and regarding a forewarned ox that killed a slave,
to be lenient and to be stringent;
regarding a rapist, a seducer, and one who defames his wife,
to be lenient and to be stringent.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new פרק right after the הדרן of פרק אין נערכין.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In four areas of law, a fixed Torah amount can work out lenient in some cases and stringent in others.

steps.title: How ערכין can be lenient or stringent
steps.stepSummary: Valuing the best-looking or the plainest person in ישראל costs the same 50 סלע, but a vow of 'his דמים' pays what the person is actually worth.
steps.simpleTranslation: How is ערכין lenient and stringent? If someone vowed the ערך of the most attractive person in ישראל or of the most unattractive person in ישראל, he gives 50 סלע. But if he said, 'His worth is on me,' he gives what that person is worth.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה explains the first item on its list, ערכין. It shows that the ערך is a fixed amount no matter who is being valued.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a good-looking person who would sell for a lot, 50 סלע is a lenient result. For a plain person who would sell for little, it is a stringent result. A vow of דמים is different: it is based on the person's real market value, not a fixed number.

keyTerms.meaning: He made a vow of ערך, the fixed Torah value of a person
Good-looking / unattractive
A coin; the Torah's ערך is counted in these
His worth: what he would sell for in the market

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up ערך and דמים. ערך is the Torah's fixed amount based on age and gender only; דמים is the real market price of the person.

phrases.english: There are, regarding valuations, cases to be lenient and stringent. How so?
Whether one valuated the most attractive person in ישראל
or the most unattractive person in ישראל,
he gives fifty סלע;
phrases.notes: This is the ערך of a man aged twenty to sixty (ויקרא 27:3).

phrases.english: but if he said: 'His worth is upon me,'
he gives his value.
phrases.notes: This means what the person would sell for as a slave, which could be more or less than 50.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the first item of the list from step 26.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A vow of ערך is a fixed 50 סלע whether the person is attractive or not; a vow of דמים pays the person's real value.

steps.title: The גמרא reads 'in ישראל' as excluding a גוי
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה and points out it says 'in ישראל', which suggests that valuing a גוי would not work.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: There are cases in ערכין to be lenient and stringent; how so? Whether one valuated... From 'in ישראל' we learn: for a Jew, yes; for גוים, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה and draws an inference from the words 'שבישראל'. This is a setup line: the inference will be used for a question in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה could have just said 'the best-looking and the plainest person.' Since it added 'in ישראל', the גמרא infers that a גוי is not included in ערכין at all. That inference is what causes trouble with רבי מאיר.

keyTerms.meaning: Yes / no: a short way of saying what is included and what is excluded
Non-Jews

phrases.english: GEMARA: There are, regarding valuations, cases to be lenient, etc.,
and to be stringent; how so? Whether one valuated, etc.
For a Jew, yes; for gentiles, no.
phrases.notes: The גמרא learns this from the extra word 'שבישראל' in the משנה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws an inference from the wording of the משנה in step 27.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From the word 'in ישראל', it seems a vow to give the ערך of a גוי does not pay the fixed amount.

steps.title: Does our משנה go against רבי מאיר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether the משנה disagrees with רבי מאיר, who taught earlier that a גוי can be valued.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say our משנה does not follow רבי מאיר? For we learned: A גוי — רבי מאיר says he can be valued, but he cannot make a vow of valuation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a problem: the inference from the last step seems to clash with an earlier משנה where רבי מאיר says a גוי can be valued.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'in ישראל' means a גוי has no ערך, then our משנה goes against רבי מאיר, who says a גוי can be valued (נערך). The next step answers this.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say: the גמרא suggests a conclusion it may not want
He can be valued: someone else can vow his ערך
He can make a vow of ערך himself

phrases.english: Shall we say our משנה is not in line with רבי מאיר?
For we learned: A gentile — רבי מאיר says:
phrases.notes: This is the משנה on daf 5b.

phrases.english: he can be valued, but he cannot make a valuation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the inference of step 28 to challenge whether the משנה fits רבי מאיר.
steps.kashyaTarget: The inference that a גוי has no ערך, which would put our משנה against רבי מאיר
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי מאיר holds a גוי is נערך; if our משנה excludes גוים from ערכין, it must disagree with him.

steps.title: The משנה can match רבי מאיר, and a non-Jew can be valued too
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the משנה can follow רבי מאיר, because a גוי can also be valued. It then starts to explain why the משנה said 'in ישראל' anyway.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can even say the משנה follows רבי מאיר. The same law applies even to a גוי as well. But [the reason the משנה said 'in ישראל' is as follows]...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 29 and says there is no argument with רבי מאיר. It ends with 'אלא' (but), which tells us it is about to explain why the משנה said 'in ישראל'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 28 the גמרא read 'in ישראל' as a hint that valuing a גוי would not work. Now it drops that reading: valuing a גוי works just the same. So the words 'in ישראל' must be there for some other reason, and the next line will give it.

keyTerms.meaning: 'You can even say': you can even say the משנה follows this person's view.
'The same law applies': the same rule covers this other case too.
A person who is not Jewish.
'Also' or 'as well'.
'But' or 'rather': here it brings in the real reason the משנה used its wording.

steps.confusionAlert: Do not stop at the word 'אלא' and think the answer is complete. The גמרא has only said a גוי can also be valued. The reason the משנה still said 'in ישראל' comes in the next line.

phrases.english: You can even say it follows Rabbi Meir;

phrases.aramaic: הוּא הַדִּין דַּאֲפִילּוּ גּוֹי נָמֵי, אֶלָּא
phrases.english: the same law applies even to a non-Jew as well, but

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 29 by dropping the inference made in step 28.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Rejects the inference from the wording: the words 'in ישראל' do not exclude a גוי. The real reason for the wording comes next.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The words 'in ישראל' meant that valuing a גוי does not work, so the משנה disagreed with רבי מאיר.
steps.terutzMaskana: Valuing a גוי also works, so the משנה fits רבי מאיר. The words 'in ישראל' serve another purpose, which the גמרא is about to explain.
